Commentary.Commentary: That's a wrap - Right then, that is it from us, with Scotland Women and Sri Lanka Women picking up dominant warm-up wins in Derby. The action continues on 8th June, Monday, where we have two warm-up matches lined up. First, it will be India Women taking on West Indies Women, beginning at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT). Then it will be the two rivals, Australia Women and hosts England Women, clashing at 2 pm GMT. You can join us early for all the build-up as well. Until then, cheers and goodbye.

We wanted to finish early - Sri Lankan skipper Chamari Athapaththu has not come out for the interview. Instead, it is her opening partner, Vishmi Gunarathne, speaking after the match. Vishmi says the wicket was good and they aimed to keep the run rate up and finish the game early. She adds that Chamari helps her a lot at the crease, constantly guiding her and giving clear instructions on what to do. Vishmi feels confident and in good touch, and says the team is looking forward to carrying this momentum forward.

The captain for Pakistan Women - Fatima Sana says she feels they struggled in the middle overs with the bat and admits they tried too many things with the ball as well. She explains that her role of coming in late to bat is a team and coaching decision, as the management feels she is more effective in the death overs. Sana mentions that the team is confident and excited about the tournament, describing it as the highest level of cricket. She also praises Chamari Athapaththu for the way she batted, acknowledging the impact she had on the game.
Let's hear from the captains now...

Pakistan left with key lessons after big defeat - Pakistan Women and Fatima Sana will take plenty of learnings from this game. They needed early wickets, but that didn’t happen, and once Sri Lanka’s ruthless attack got going, they had no answers at all. The biggest difference came in the hitting power, with Pakistan managing just one six in their innings, while Sri Lanka struck eight, a telling gap in modern T20 cricket. Fatima Sana did manage to pick up a wicket, but by then the game had already slipped away. The bigger concern will be the effectiveness of their spinners, something they will need to assess closely going forward.

Momentum swings both ways - Earlier in the game, Pakistan Women got off to a strong start with the openers racing to 53 in the powerplay and building a solid 60-run stand. Sri Lanka then pulled things back with regular wickets to reduce them to 105/6, but skipper Fatima Sana's 37 off 26, along with Aliya Riaz’s support, lifted Pakistan to a competitive total. Chethana Vimukthi was the pick of the bowlers with a brilliant four-wicket haul, well supported by Malki Madara, Nimasha Meepage and Sugandika Kumari, as Sri Lanka fought back strongly after a slow Powerplay but kept Pakistan within reach of a competitive finish.

Athapaththu falls short of ton but dominates - A few would have thought this would be a stiff target, but the Sri Lankan openers had other ideas. They went all guns blazing right from ball one, sparing none and smashing 64 in the Powerplay. The fielding restrictions didn’t change anything as they kept going after the bowlers, with both batters bringing up their respective fifties. Chamari Athapaththu shifted gears impressively, peppering the mid-wicket region and taking her side close to the win. She eventually fell short of her century on 94, but the 160-run opening stand had already killed the game, and fittingly, Vishmi Gunarathne stayed unbeaten on 63 to hit the winning runs.

Statement win for Sri Lanka Women - Despite this being a warm-up game, Sri Lanka, apart from the first six overs with the ball, completely outplayed Pakistan Women across all three departments. It was a dominant all-round display that will give them plenty of confidence heading into the tournament. Pakistan, on the other hand, will need to go back to the drawing board and find a way to adapt better to English conditions, which they have yet to fully get to grips with.

SRI LANKA WIN BY 9 WICKETS! A comfortable finish in the end. A length delivery around leg stump, and Vishmi Gunarathne calmly clips it down to deep fine leg for a single. That is all they need as Sri Lanka complete the chase with ease, getting home with nine balls to spare.
